purpose: Add two matching sinusoidal waves and connect phase difference to the resulting amplitude.
meaning: Slide one wave relative to the other. Their point-by-point sum changes continuously from reinforcement to cancellation and back.

research_tasks: Research the concept and notation with specialist sources before adding historical attribution.

Superposition is linear; contributions are measured in the same units.
The phase control is in radians, from 0 to 2π.

definition.setting: Add two matching sinusoidal waves and connect phase difference to the resulting amplitude.

signature.A: equal nonnegative amplitude of each source

conditions: Both component waves have the same frequency, wave number, amplitude and propagation direction.
Superposition is linear; contributions are measured in the same units.
The phase control is in radians, from 0 to 2π.
definition.domain_notes: This equal-wave model is a simplified local signal description; amplitude 0.2–2 units. R is amplitude, not energy, intensity or loudness.
definition.proof_status: Apply sin u+sin v=2sin((u+v)/2)cos((u−v)/2) and take the coefficient magnitude.

grammar.pronunciation: The resultant amplitude is twice the source amplitude times the absolute cosine of half the relative phase.
grammar.formation_rule: Output=2*amplitude*abs(cos(phase/2)). The drawn signed sum is A*sin(u)+A*sin(u+phase); the output reports its nonnegative amplitude.
grammar.precedence: Follow parentheses and function applications; products precede sums. Angle units and iteration conventions are explicit.
